distractorExplanations.b: Homestead is a separate protection of a residence from certain creditors, not a feature of joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.c: Reversion is the grantor's future interest after a life estate, unrelated to co-ownership rights.

prompt: A metes-and-bounds description starts at a:

options.text: Point of beginning
Township number
Lot number in a condo declaration
Assessor parcel map without courses

explanation: Metes and bounds walks courses and distances from a point of beginning.

distractorExplanations.b: Granular rectangular survey uses townships/sections.
distractorExplanations.c: Lot/block is a different description system.
distractorExplanations.d: APNs identify parcels but aren't metes-and-bounds courses.

prompt: Police power in land-use control includes:

options.text: Only private deed restrictions
Zoning and building codes
Only mortgage foreclosure
Only federal income tax liens

explanation: Zoning and building codes are classic police-power land-use tools.

distractorExplanations.a: CC&Rs are private.
distractorExplanations.c: Foreclosure is a creditor remedy.
distractorExplanations.d: Tax liens are different.

prompt: Eminent domain requires:

options.text: Public use and the owner's written consent
Just compensation set by the county assessor
Public use/purpose and just compensation
A court finding that the owner is delinquent on taxes

explanation: Takings require public purpose and just compensation under the Constitution. This framework comes from the Fifth Amendment.

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is the government's power to take without consent; only just compensation is owed to the owner.
distractorExplanations.b: Compensation is fair market value set by negotiation or the court, not the assessor's tax value; public use is also required.
distractorExplanations.d: Tax delinquency leads to a tax sale, a different process; eminent domain needs public use and compensation.

prompt: Which of the following best describes rescission as tested on this exam?

options.text: Unqualified agreement to terms of offer communicated as required.
Proposal to enter contract on definite terms communicated to offeree.
Contract setting terms for transfer of property from seller to buyer.
Canceling contract and restoring parties to pre-contract positions

explanation: Canceling contract and restoring parties to pre-contract positions. Example: Buyer rescinds due to misrepresentation.

distractorExplanations.a: Not the best answer here; the right answer is “Canceling contract and restoring parties to pre-contract positions”.
distractorExplanations.b: Not the best answer here; the right answer is “Canceling contract and restoring parties to pre-contract positions”.
distractorExplanations.c: Not the best answer here; the right answer is “Canceling contract and restoring parties to pre-contract positions”.

prompt: A listing broker's primary fiduciary duty to the seller client is to: (applied scenario 2)

options.text: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law
Obtain the highest possible price even when the seller instructs a quicker sale
Represent both parties equally once the buyer signs a purchase agreement
Disclose the seller's lowest acceptable price to buyers to speed negotiations

explanation: Agency duties center on loyalty and obedience to lawful client instructions, not guaranteeing outcomes.

distractorExplanations.b: Obedience to lawful instructions outranks the agent's own price goal; a seller may prioritize speed or terms over top price.
distractorExplanations.c: Equal representation of both sides is dual agency and requires disclosure and consent; signing an offer does not create it.
distractorExplanations.d: Revealing the seller's bottom line breaches the duties of loyalty and confidentiality owed to the seller client.

prompt: In California contracts, when must a licensee typically disclose a dual agency or designated agency relationship?

options.text: At closing, when the final settlement statement is reviewed and signed by both parties
Before or as soon as practicable when the dual/designated relationship arises
When the first offer is drafted, even if the relationship began earlier
Within five days after the purchase contract is accepted by the seller

explanation: Agency disclosure timing is early—when the dual or designated relationship is created or contemplated. Follow the applicable state agency-disclosure rules for the exact form and timing.

distractorExplanations.a: Disclosure at closing is too late; consent must be informed before the dual or designated relationship affects negotiations.
distractorExplanations.c: Waiting until an offer is written is too late if the dual or designated relationship already arose at a showing or earlier.
distractorExplanations.d: Invents a post-acceptance grace period; disclosure comes before or as soon as practicable when the relationship arises, not after acceptance.

prompt: An exclusive right-to-sell listing generally means:

options.text: The listing broker is owed a commission unless the seller personally finds the buyer during the term
The seller may list with several brokers and pays a commission only to the broker who procures the buyer
The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer
The broker keeps any sale proceeds above the seller's stated minimum price as the commission

explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell typically protects the listing broker's commission if a sale occurs during the listing term. The exact protection follows the terms of the listing agreement.

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing, where the seller keeps the right to sell without owing a commission.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes an open listing, where only the procuring broker is paid and the seller may also sell directly.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a net listing, which concerns how the commission is calculated, not exclusivity of the right to sell.

prompt: Earnest money is best described as:

options.text: The buyer's down payment, which the lender holds until the loan closes
Consideration required to make a purchase contract valid and binding
A deposit the listing broker may treat as commission once the offer is accepted
A good-faith deposit typically held in escrow/trust pending contract performance

explanation: Earnest money shows good faith and is usually escrowed subject to the contract.

distractorExplanations.a: Earnest money is usually credited toward the down payment but is held by the broker or escrow, not the lender.
distractorExplanations.b: Mutual promises are sufficient consideration; earnest money is not legally required for a valid contract.
distractorExplanations.c: Earnest money stays in trust until closing or release; applying it to commission early is conversion.

prompt: A material fact that must typically be disclosed to a buyer includes:

options.text: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability
The seller's reasons for selling and the lowest price the seller is willing to accept
The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood surrounding the property
That a former occupant of the home was living with HIV or AIDS

explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared; confidential motivations may be protected. Disclosure duties follow applicable law.

distractorExplanations.b: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts.
distractorExplanations.c: Discussing neighborhood racial or religious composition is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: HIV/AIDS is a protected disability under federal fair housing law; it is not a material property fact to disclose.

prompt: If a buyer customer asks a listing agent for advice on how much to offer, the listing agent should

options.text: Suggest an offer amount, since helping the buyer also helps close the sale
Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role
Share the seller's lowest acceptable price so the buyer can offer efficiently
Give a price opinion as long as the buyer has signed the agency disclosure form

explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift/disclosure. If allowed, the brokerage may properly create buyer agency with required disclosures.

distractorExplanations.a: Recommending an offer amount is buyer advocacy that conflicts with the listing agent's loyalty to the seller.
distractorExplanations.c: Revealing the seller's bottom line breaches the confidentiality duty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.d: Signing an agency disclosure does not create buyer representation; the agent still represents only the seller.

prompt: A contract is generally voidable by a party who:

options.text: Later found a better price elsewhere
Signed without an earnest money deposit
Was induced by fraud or was a minor
Was adjudged incompetent before signing

explanation: Fraud or lack of capacity can make a contract voidable by the protected party. Whether the contract is voidable depends on the circumstances (e.g., ratification after reaching majority).

distractorExplanations.a: Buyer's remorse or a better deal elsewhere is not a legal ground to avoid a contract; fraud or incapacity is.
distractorExplanations.b: Earnest money is not required for a valid contract; consideration can be the mutual promises, so its absence does not make it voidable.
distractorExplanations.d: A contract by someone already adjudged incompetent by a court is void, not voidable; voidable applies to minors and fraud victims.

prompt: Private mortgage insurance (PMI) is most often required when:

options.text: An FHA loan is made with a 3.5% down payment
A VA loan is made with zero down payment to a veteran
Conventional LTV is low (commonly below 80%)
Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)

explanation: PMI protects conventional lenders when down payment/equity is thin.

distractorExplanations.a: FHA loans carry FHA mortgage insurance premiums (MIP), not private mortgage insurance; PMI is a conventional-loan product.
distractorExplanations.b: VA loans have no monthly mortgage insurance; the VA guaranty and funding fee take its place, so PMI does not apply.
distractorExplanations.c: Reverses the threshold; PMI is triggered when the conventional LTV exceeds 80%, and borrowers at or below 80% LTV usually avoid it.

prompt: An adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM) interest rate:

options.text: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps
Can adjust based on the margin alone, with the index fixed
Can adjust at the lender's discretion, with no caps
Is fixed for the loan term but payments can rise with taxes

explanation: ARMs adjust with index + margin within contractual caps.

distractorExplanations.b: Inverts the formula: the margin is the fixed part set at origination, while the index moves and drives rate changes.
distractorExplanations.c: ARM changes follow a published index under the note, and periodic and lifetime caps limit how far the rate can move.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes a fixed-rate loan with escrow changes; an ARM's interest rate itself resets periodically based on index plus margin.

prompt: Title insurance primarily protects against:

options.text: Physical damage to the home from fire, flood, or other casualty
Covered title defects and claims against ownership per the policy
Losses to the lender if the borrower later defaults on the mortgage note
Defects and liens that arise after the policy date at closing

explanation: Owner's/lender's title policies insure against covered title risks, not casualty.

distractorExplanations.a: Casualty loss is covered by hazard (homeowner's) insurance; title insurance covers defects in title, not physical damage.
distractorExplanations.c: Default risk is covered by mortgage insurance (PMI/MIP); a lender's title policy protects the lien's validity and priority, not repayment.
distractorExplanations.d: Title policies look backward: they insure against covered defects existing at the policy date, not liens created afterward.

prompt: A debit to the buyer on a closing statement means:

options.text: The buyer is credited; it reduces cash needed
The item is split evenly between buyer and seller
The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed
The lender pays it; it reduces the loan amount

explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. For the seller, a debit reduces sale proceeds.

distractorExplanations.a: Reverses the entries: a credit reduces what the buyer owes, while a debit is a charge to the buyer.
distractorExplanations.b: Splits are prorations or negotiated sharing, shown as separate debits to each party, not the meaning of a debit.
distractorExplanations.d: A buyer debit is a charge to the buyer; lender-paid items appear as credits, and the loan amount is unchanged.

prompt: The secondary mortgage market's main function is to:

options.text: Originate purchase loans directly to borrowers at retail branches
Set the federal funds rate that drives mortgage interest rates
Insure lenders against borrower default on high-LTV conventional loans
Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity for originators

explanation: Entities like Fannie/Freddie (and others) provide liquidity by purchasing loans.

distractorExplanations.a: Origination happens in the primary mortgage market; the secondary market buys loans after they are made.
distractorExplanations.b: The Federal Reserve sets monetary policy and the federal funds rate; the secondary market buys and pools existing mortgages.
distractorExplanations.c: That is the role of private mortgage insurers; secondary-market entities such as Fannie Mae buy loans to supply liquidity.

prompt: Usury laws generally regulate:

options.text: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans
Minimum disclosures of loan costs such as the APR to borrowers
Kickbacks and referral fees among settlement service providers
Lending discrimination based on race, sex, or marital status

explanation: Usury caps address excessive interest.

distractorExplanations.b: Cost disclosure such as APR is governed by the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), not usury laws, which cap the interest rate.
distractorExplanations.c: Kickbacks and unearned referral fees are prohibited by RESPA Section 8; usury laws address maximum interest charges.
distractorExplanations.d: Credit discrimination is barred by the Equal Credit Opportunity Act; usury laws limit how much interest a lender may charge.

prompt: A bridge loan is typically used to:

options.text: Fund construction in stages through draws, then convert to a permanent loan once the home is finished
Finance a short-term gap, often between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one
Combine a first mortgage and a second loan to avoid PMI on a new home purchase
Refinance an existing home to lower the rate over a new 30-year amortizing term

explanation: Bridge (swing) financing covers short gaps in housing transitions.

distractorExplanations.a: Describes a construction-to-permanent loan with staged draws; a bridge loan is a short-term gap loan tied to a home sale.
distractorExplanations.c: Describes a piggyback (80-10-10) loan structure used to avoid PMI, not a temporary gap loan between two homes.
distractorExplanations.d: A rate-and-term refinance is long-term permanent financing; a bridge loan is short-term and repaid when the old home sells.

prompt: On a fully amortizing fixed-rate mortgage, what does each level monthly payment primarily cover over the life of the loan?

options.text: Both interest and principal so the unpaid balance declines to zero by maturity
Interest only for the term, with the full principal due as a balloon at maturity
Equal principal portions each month, so the interest portion stays level
Mostly principal in the early years and mostly interest near the end of the term

explanation: Fully amortizing fixed-rate payments are calculated to pay interest and reduce principal across the term.

distractorExplanations.b: Describes an interest-only (term) loan with a balloon payment; a fully amortizing loan retires principal with each payment.
distractorExplanations.c: Reverses the mix: on a level payment, the interest portion falls and the principal portion grows over the life of the loan.
distractorExplanations.d: Backwards: early payments are mostly interest because the balance is highest; the principal share grows toward maturity.

prompt: RESPA's core consumer-protection theme includes:

options.text: Requiring APR disclosure and a right of rescission on certain refinance loans
Prohibiting lending discrimination based on race, religion, sex, or marital status
Requiring lenders to report mortgage application data by census tract to detect redlining patterns
Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures in covered transactions

explanation: RESPA addresses settlement services, kickbacks, and related disclosures (with TRID integration for many loans).

distractorExplanations.a: APR disclosure and the right of rescission come from the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), not RESPA's kickback and settlement rules.
distractorExplanations.b: Lending discrimination is barred by the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Fair Housing Act; RESPA targets settlement costs and kickbacks.
distractorExplanations.c: Describes the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA); RESPA bans kickbacks and requires settlement cost disclosures.

prompt: A conventional loan that is not insured/guaranteed by FHA/VA/USDA is typically called:

options.text: A conventional loan
A government loan
A reverse bridge grant
A hard-money gift letter

explanation: Conventional loans lack FHA/VA/USDA insurance/guarantee.

distractorExplanations.b: Opposite category.
distractorExplanations.c: Not a standard term here.
distractorExplanations.d: Gift letters document gifts; hard money is private lending.

prompt: If annual property taxes are $3,600 and the seller owned the property for 3 months of the tax year at closing (buyer pays full year later), a typical proration if seller owes buyer for prepaid/advance assumptions depends on custom—but the monthly tax amount is
explanation: $3,600 ÷ 12 = $300 per month—the unit used in many proration setups.

distractorExplanations.a: That is the annual amount.
distractorExplanations.c: Too low.
distractorExplanations.d: That would be 4 months.

prompt: A prepayment penalty clause:

options.text: Requires extra payment if the borrower makes a payment more than 15 days late
Lets the borrower pay off early with no charge, when the note allows it
Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early, when the note allows it
Lets the lender demand full payoff if the borrower sells the property

explanation: Prepayment penalties charge for early payoff when permitted by the loan terms and law.

distractorExplanations.a: Describes a late charge triggered by a missed due date; a prepayment penalty applies when the loan is paid off ahead of schedule.
distractorExplanations.b: Describes a prepayment privilege (open) clause, the opposite of a penalty; a prepayment penalty adds a charge for early payoff.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes a due-on-sale (alienation) clause; a prepayment penalty is a charge for paying the loan off early.

prompt: Private mortgage insurance (PMI) is most often required when: (applied scenario 2)

options.text: An FHA loan is made with a 3.5% down payment
A VA loan is made with zero down payment to a veteran
Conventional LTV is low (commonly below 80%)
Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)

explanation: PMI protects conventional lenders when down payment/equity is thin.

distractorExplanations.a: FHA loans carry FHA mortgage insurance premiums (MIP), not private mortgage insurance; PMI is a conventional-loan product.
distractorExplanations.b: VA loans have no monthly mortgage insurance; the VA guaranty and funding fee take its place, so PMI does not apply.
distractorExplanations.c: Reverses the threshold; PMI is triggered when the conventional LTV exceeds 80%, and borrowers at or below 80% LTV usually avoid it.
